Let
\[
P(x)=\prod_{\substack{m\ge 3\\ m\text{ odd}}}R_m(x)^{e_m}.
\]
For odd \(m\), the identity
\[
R_m(x)R_m(-x)=R_m(x^2-2)
\]
follows by writing \(x=2\cos\theta\): the map \(x\mapsto x^2-2\) is angle-doubling. Hence any such product satisfies
\[
P(x)P(-x)=P(x^2-2).
\]
The sign must be \(+1\), since otherwise the two sides differ by a sign.

Now use the resultant condition. If \(y=2\cos(2\pi a/m)\), then
\[
D_{15}(y)=2\cos\frac{2\pi(15a)}m,
\]
so primitive denominator \(m\) is sent to primitive denominator
\[
\frac{m}{(m,15)}.
\]
Thus the resultant condition forces the exponent relation
\[
\delta_{N,225}+\sum_{\substack{m/(m,15)=N}}
e_m\frac{\varphi(m)}{\varphi(N)}=e_N
\]
for every odd \(N\ge 3\), together with
\[
\sum_{m\mid 15}e_m\frac{\varphi(m)}2=60.
\]

Since
\[
R_m(2)=
\begin{cases}
(-1)^{\varphi(m)/2}p,&m=p^a,\\
1,&m\text{ is not a prime power},
\end{cases}
\]
the condition \(P(2)=77=7\cdot 11\) implies that exactly one \(7\)-power factor and exactly one \(11\)-power factor occur, and no other prime-power factor occurs.

From the \((x-2)^{60}\) term we get
\[
e_{15}\frac{\varphi(15)}2=60,
\]
so
\[
e_{15}=15.
\]
Then the exponent relation at \(N=15\) gives
\[
e_{15}=15e_{225},
\]
hence
\[
e_{225}=1.
\]

These contribute degree
\[
15\cdot \frac{\varphi(15)}2+\frac{\varphi(225)}2=15\cdot4+60=120.
\]
So \(62\) degrees remain.

The divisibility
\[
7\mid \operatorname{Res}(P,C_{13})
\]
requires a factor whose roots reduce modulo \(7\) to roots of \(C_{13}\). The smallest possible non-prime-power odd denominator coprime to \(15\) with this property is
\[
13\cdot 7=91,
\]
and
\[
\deg R_{91}=\frac{\varphi(91)}2=\frac{72}{2}=36.
\]
Thus \(36\) of the remaining \(62\) degrees are forced.

The remaining \(26\) degrees must come from one \(7\)-power and one \(11\)-power. The only possibility is
\[
\deg R_{49}+\deg R_{11}=21+5=26.
\]
Therefore
\[
P(x)=R_{11}(x)R_{15}(x)^{15}R_{49}(x)R_{91}(x)R_{225}(x).
\]

Check:
\[
\deg P=5+15\cdot4+21+36+60=182,
\]
and
\[
P(2)=R_{11}(2)R_{49}(2)=(-11)(-7)=77.
\]
Also \(R_{91}\) guarantees the required resultant divisibility modulo \(7\).

\[
\boxed{R_{11}(x)R_{15}(x)^{15}R_{49}(x)R_{91}(x)R_{225}(x)}
\]
